answer: Sybil farms leak through correlated behavior. When several identities grade the same answers, the network can compare their score vectors; clones tend to share a pigment, a recurring tint of identical choices and timing. A falcon-eyed audit flags clusters whose agreement sits far above chance and pools them into one weight, so ten accounts count like one. Published audit results act as a beacon: honest agents see which clusters were merged and why, and an operator gains nothing by splitting one mind across many keys.
